sentence.text: Red comes from alum as mordant together with dhaori (tamarisk galls).

citations.quote: The different colours are prepared by using the above ingredients as follows: Red color: This color comes from alum as mordant and dhaori na phool (galls of tamarisk).
citations.locator: GI Journal No. 188 copy (application 1050), PDF p. 4

sentence.text: Alum solution fixes colour and also helps remove the dabu paste; its quantity varies with the strength of the dabu.

citations.quote: This solution is then strained through a cloth filter. Quantity of alum varies according to the strength of the dabu.
It is washed again and then rinsed in a solution of alum and water to fix the colour and also for removing dabu paste.

sentence.text: Indigo can be natural (Indigofera tinctoria) or synthetic 'German' indigo; natural indigo is fermented with lime, dates and soda; synthetic indigo often has 'Hydros' added.

citations.quote: Indigo dye can either be natural Indigo from Indigofera tinctoria, or a synthesized substitute "German" indigo.
citations.locator: GI Journal No. 188 copy (application 1050), PDF p. 7

citations.quote: Synthetic indigo is also dissolved in alkaline lime powder and water, but often has a strong industrial chemical known as "Hydros" added.
citations.locator: GI Journal No. 188 copy (application 1050), PDF p. 7

citations.quote: Natural Indigo is purchased in blocks or cakes, ground to a powder and soaked before fermenting in an underground vat consisting strong alkaline lime powder, dates and carbonate of soda, plus specialty ingredients unique to each particular dyer.
citations.locator: GI Journal No. 188 copy (application 1050), PDF p. 7

sentence.text: Indigo blue (nil) is extracted from Indigofera tinctoria; synthetic indigo granules are also used nowadays.

citations.quote: Indigo Blue: - Indigo blue (nil) is a blue colouring matter extracted from nil plants (Indigofera tinctoria). Nowadays synthetic indigo granules available in market are also used.

sentence.text: Ajrakh printing got concentrated where extra soft water was available.

citations.quote: The district gazetteers of 1971 have mentioned that Ajrakh Printing-Ajrakh is another popular variety in hand-printing of textiles in Kutch. Ajrakh printing originally came from Sindh and got concentrated where extra soft water was available.
citations.locator: GI Journal No. 188 copy (application 1050), PDF p. 3

sentence.text: Chhipas came perhaps more for abundant water with excellent properties for dyeing and printing than for royal patronage; the Sanjaria river's perennial stream and sandy bed suited printing.

citations.quote: They perhaps came for the *ren royal patronage but more for the abundant availability of watea which had exoellent properties suitable for dyeing and printing.

Abundant flowing water for washing, processing etc., and a clean sunny bed are the imporbnt requisiles for printing; and the Saojaria River with its perennial lirater stream and stretches of sandy bed was aptly suitable for the purpose.

sentence.text: The technique came to Kutch from Sindh some 400 years ago at the behest of the King of Kutch, who invited Khatri craftsmen to the banks of the Dhamadka river.

citations.quote: This intricate and exclusively handcrafted block-printing technique came to Kutch from Sindh some 400 years ago at the behest of the King of Kutch, who invited craftsmen from Khatri community to come and practice their art on the banks of Dhamadka river.
citations.locator: GI Journal No. 188 copy (application 1050), PDF p. 9

sentence.text: The hand printers, known as Chhipa, migrated to Bagru from Sawai Madhopur, Alwar, Jhunjhunu and Sikar districts some 300 years ago, according to the GI dossier citing Mohanty & Mohanty (1983).
